attributions.rationale: The phrase "the next parliament" orders parliament as the next countable election-bounded instance, so sense:002 is natural. Sense:001 denotes the continuing institution and does not itself supply the succession implied by "next".

In "during this parliament", the preposition "during" and demonstrative "this" make parliament the bounded interval within which the measure will be introduced, selecting sense:002. Sense:001 is a standing institution, not the delimited span picked out here.

The construction "the lifetime of a parliament" assigns a finite lifespan to one countable parliament, directly selecting sense:002. The continuing institution in sense:001 may persist across elections and therefore is not the entity whose lifetime measures completion here.

The zero-article institutional complement in "member of parliament" names the body in which she holds elected membership, selecting sense:001. A particular election-bounded instance under sense:002 would require language that identifies that instance or its term, which this membership formula lacks.

discriminating_terms: The Scottish Parliament passed the bill
attributions.rationale: In "The Scottish Parliament passed the bill", the official institutional name is the collective legislative agent performing enactment, which selects sense:001. Nothing in parliament's use numbers an elected iteration or measures an election-to-election period, so sense:002 is not licensed by the headword phrase.

The complement "before Parliament" treats Parliament as the institutional forum considering the bill, selecting sense:001. Sense:002 would require a particular elected parliament or its bounded duration to be the relevant referent, but neither is expressed in this headword construction.

The phrase "during the current parliament" locates passage within the presently running, bounded parliamentary term, so sense:002 is selected. The continuing institution in sense:001 is not made "current" in contrast with a preceding or following iteration.

The fixed institutional-destination frame "elected to Parliament" describes entry into the legislature and thus selects sense:001. Sense:002 would make the election result a particular iteration or term, whereas the zero-article proper-name complement here denotes the institution joined.

The formal expression "an Act of Parliament" identifies Parliament as the institutional legislative source of the Act, selecting sense:001. It does not identify the lifetime or numbered elected body required for sense:002.

discriminating_terms: The general election produced a hung parliament
attributions.rationale: In "The general election produced a hung parliament", parliament is the new countable body resulting from that election, directly selecting sense:002. Sense:001 is the continuing institution and is not itself produced anew by the stated general election.
